notes: The copula was of A Syrian ready to perish was my father goes to the nominal predicate under rule 20; the alternative of attaching it to the attributive participle was available but the predicate's head noun is the better anchor, and the explicit subject ʾāḇî takes only its own English.

few in number is split morpheme by morpheme: bə takes in, mᵉṯê takes number and mᵉʿāṭ takes few. The competing reading takes the whole phrase as one indivisible rendering of mᵉṯê mᵉʿāṭ, but each Hebrew word holds an English word of its own, so rule 2 splits it.
The resultative lə before gôy is unrepresented because hāyāh itself carries became (rules 21, 40).
